passages.original: 5. [1642] Lameeh, annorum CLXXXX, genuit Noe, qui divino oraeulo arcam aedifieare juhetur, anno aetatis suæ quiogentesimo. His temporibus, ut refert Josephus, scientes illi homines quod aut igne, aut aquit, perire poterant, in duabus coiumnis, ex latere et lapide factis, studia sua conscripserunt, ne deleretur memoria eorum quae sapienter invenerant.
passages.english: 5. [1642] Lamech, at 190 years, fathered Noah, who by a divine oracle was ordered to build the ark, in the five hundredth year of his age. In these times, as Josephus reports, those men, knowing that they could perish either by fire or by water, wrote down their studies on two columns, made of brick and of stone, so that the memory of the things they had wisely discovered should not be destroyed.
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected silently (oraeulo = oraculo, aedifieare = aedificare, juhetur = jubetur, quiogentesimo = quingentesimo, aquit = aqua, coiumnis = columnis). The bracketed number [1642] is the edition's running year of the world. Lamech's age is given as 190, not the Hebrew figure of 182; the numeral is left as it stands.

passages.original: 6. [2242] Noe anno sexcentesimo factum legitur diluvium, cujus arcam Josephus sedisse refert in montes Armeniae, qui vocantur 67 Ararat. Fuerunt autem Noe filii tres, ex quibus septuaginta duæ gentes sunt ortae, id est, quindecim de Jephet, triginta de Gham, viginti septem de Sem.
passages.english: 6. [2242] In Noah's six hundredth year, we read, the flood took place; Josephus reports that his ark settled on the mountains of Armenia, which are called Ararat. Noah had three sons, from whom seventy-two nations arose, that is, fifteen from Japheth, thirty from Ham, twenty-seven from Shem.
passages.notes: The stray '67' before Ararat is probably a page or column number from the printed edition and has been omitted. The figure 2242 is the edition's year of the world.
